title: Sopra Steria UK's central-government incumbency buys access but not partnership
content:
Sopra Steria UK is recorded as a major UK central-government incumbent, and the verdict is compressed to four words: access yes, partnership no. The stack is Microsoft and Salesforce, the same proprietary pairing as the Dutch entity, and the priority is the same 9.

Incumbency in central government is the strongest possible route to the buyers this thesis cares about, which is exactly what makes the row instructive. Being inside the departments where sovereign, auditable record-keeping is a live requirement does not make a firm a carrier for someone else's layer. An incumbent's commercial interest is continuity of its existing programmes and the platforms those programmes are built on.

Taken with the Dutch row, the two Sopra Steria entries make the finding a pattern rather than a one-off: the same firm, two countries, two independent assessments, and both land on access without partnership. That symmetry is worth more than either row alone, because it shows the inversion is a property of the incumbent-supplier model rather than of a particular national practice.
